## Image 1 — Sheathed frames (3)

**Per-frame arm trace** (all 3 frames are essentially identical):

1. **Sword/right arm:** shoulder (chest) → elbow travels forward and slightly down in front of the ribcage → hand drops vertically below the elbow. Elbow interior angle ≈ **90–100°**, fold direction is **forward/down**. ✔ No hyperextension, no backward bend.
2. **Off/left arm:** overlapping the right chain in side view; same geometry, same forward fold. ✔
3. **Pommel contact: FAIL.** The hand hangs in **mid-air in front of the belly/stomach**, not on the hilt at the hip. There is no visible contact with a scabbard/pommel point, and no sword geometry at the hip at all. The "sheathed" read is not achieved — the arm looks like it's holding an invisible tray.
4. **Other defects:** no backward elbow, no hand-inside-pelvis, no dislocation read. Minor issue: the hand terminus slightly overlaps the torso silhouette, which reads as "floating against the belly" rather than gripping anything.

**Verdict: STILL BROKEN** — elbow kinematics fixed, but the pose intent failed: right hand floats in front of the abdomen instead of resting on the hilt/pommel at the hip. Contact target needs to move down ~1 torso-unit and aft toward the pelvis.

## Image 2 — Safe idle, sword drawn low (4)

**Per-frame arm trace:**

1. **Sword/right arm:** shoulder → elbow forward at waist height → hand below elbow. Angle ≈ **95–110°**, fold **forward/down**. ✔ All 4 frames consistent, no frame flips the fold.
2. **Off/left arm:** same chain, same forward fold, slightly higher elbow in bottom-row frames (natural idle variance). ✔
3. **Hilt contact: FAIL** (same as Image 1, slightly better). Hand hangs in front of the lower belly — closer to hip height than Image 1, and plausibly near where a low-held sword grip would be, but **no visible sword/hilt geometry** and no contact point, so it still reads as an empty hanging hand.
4. **Other defects:** none — no backward elbow, no pelvis collapse, no dislocation, no torso-crossing. Bottom-right frame shows the hand marginally deeper toward the body line; watch it, but it's outside the silhouette.

**Verdict: STILL BROKEN (marginal)** — arm kinematics are fixed and stable across all 4 frames, but the drawn-sword contact is unconvincing: add visible blade/hilt geometry anchored to the right hand, or it reads as idle-with-nothing.

## Summary
| Check | Image 1 | Image 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Elbow fold forward/down | ✔ all frames | ✔ all frames |
| No hyperextension (~172°) | ✔ fixed | ✔ fixed |
| Hand on hilt/pommel | ✘ floats at belly | ✘ near-hip but no contact/geometry |
| Dislocation / pelvis collapse | ✔ none | ✔ none |

**Root cause of remaining failure is contact/target placement, not IK:** retarget the right-hand IK goal to a hip-anchored pommel socket (Image 1) and parent a sword prop to the right hand (Image 2).

The hand hangs in front of belly, not at hip/pommel; no sword visible. Also arms look like hands floating in front of torso, not resting on hip — the "sheathed" contact isn't achieved. And in Image 1 the arms are identical across frames and not touching hip. So Image 1: STILL BROKEN (contact failure, hand floats mid-torso, no pommel contact) though elbow geometry OK. Image 2: similar—hand in front of abdomen, not low at hip; elbows fine. Verdicts.

Also check: is hand inside pelvis? Hand is slightly in front of torso, appears overlapping silhouette near belly — partially overlapping but not inside pelvis. Elbow angle ~90-100°, folding forward — OK.
